_why: Role track for PAINTER / POWDER COATING, authored under docs/profiling/role-pack-authoring-guide.md as a Batch 2 pack. fam_painting is HOUSE PAINTING -- walls, putty, distemper, a brush and a ladder -- and shares nothing with an industrial coating hand beyond the English word 'painter'. Reusing that family or its pack id would ask a man who runs a conveyorised powder line about wall putty, so the ids are fam_powder_coating / qp_powder_coating, named for the half of the trade that is unambiguous. Only the industrial coating occupations belong here; the construction painter keeps fam_painting's own interview, whose first question already disambiguates him.
_scope: POWDER AND LIQUID SPRAY, on the same ruling that shaped qp_cnc_turning and qp_cnc_grinding. The ratified sheet's own worker runs both -- 'Powder coating, Liquid spray -- HVLP, Electrostatic spray' is his headline -- and a paint-shop hand who has only ever held an HVLP gun must be able to answer every question here honestly: coating_process leads with powder coating but carries liquid spray and touch-up beside it, coating_equipment carries the spray booth next to the powder booth, and booth_type has a 'Pata nahi' escape. The gate says 'Powder coating ya paint', not 'Powder coating', for the same reason the turner's gate says 'Turning'.
_depth: THE TIER GATE IS coating_experience, asked FIRST, and it is the key PAINTER_COATING.tenureQuestionKey already names. It cannot be experience_years from qp_universal: phase order runs occupation_specific BEFORE universal_tail, so the universal answer does not exist yet when these items are selected -- and a worker handed the role form on his first message may never be asked it at all. Its options carry value_number ONLY. pack-registry.service.ts resolves valueText ?? valueNumber ?? valueBool, so adding a value_text would make the captured answer a STRING; every gte below would then compare a string to a number, compare() returns null, and the predicate is false forever. A permanently-false ask_if is a question that is never asked, silently -- the #776 defect that sat in qp_welding for the life of the pack. The ask_if shape here is {op, left:{field}, right:{const}}, never {op, args:[...]}, which is the same defect wearing the other hat.
_budget: MAX_ENGINE_ASKS is 28 and qp_universal spends 8. Tier 0 is 8 items (16 total), tier 1 adds 3 (19), tier 2 adds 4 (23). The three fresher items are gated on coating_experience <= 0 and a senior never sees them; a fresher skips tiers 1 and 2 entirely, so his worst case is 16 + 3 = 19. The tiers are mutually exclusive by construction, which is why the fresher branch costs the senior nothing. qp_universal@2 already asks primary_trade, experience_years, current_city, salary_expected, preferred_locations, availability, education and shift_preference; none of them is repeated here.
_sheet: SECTION B IS READ OFF THE RATIFIED REFERENCE SHEET (Shyam Lal Meena, Painter / Powder Coating -- Skilled), not invented. Its eight rows are Processes, Equipment, Coatings applied, Surface preparation, Checks performed, Film thickness held, Booth type and Sector worked, and every one has a question here that fills it: coating_process, coating_equipment, coating_material, surface_prep, coating_checks, film_thickness, booth_type, sector_worked. FILM THICKNESS IS A BANDED single_select rather than a free number -- the sheet prints '60 - 80 microns', which is a band, and a banded chip keeps a low-literacy worker tapping instead of typing while avoiding the answer_type 'number' path that has no Flutter widget. SURFACE PREPARATION CARRIES EIGHT CHIPS AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: the ratified row has seven ticks (Degreasing, Phosphating, Shot blasting, Sanding, Masking, Hanging & jigging, Oven schedule setting) and all seven must be offerable or the row cannot be filled, so the eighth is the none-of-above a man whose prep is done by another gang needs. THE LEVEL RUNG IS ITS OWN QUESTION: every reference sheet leads with '{Role} -- {Level}' and this one reads 'Painter / Powder Coating -- Skilled', so coating_level offers exactly PAINTER_COATING.levelLadder and nothing else. It is NOT a Section B row and is absent from the resume map -- the rung prints in the headline, not in the capability block.
review_note: Drafted for owner review (Prakash). Shop-floor vocabulary NOT yet corrected by a practising powder coater -- see docs/registers/trade-content-ratification.md.
_fresher: Guideline section 11 #1: a fresher's Zone 4 is training, trade test, machines used in the ITI workshop and project work, and the History heading never renders empty. These three items are the ask half; resume-fresher-rows.ts, fed by this role's descriptor, is the render half, and it reads iti_workshop_machines and trade_test_status LITERALLY -- the keys are not renameable. Only the OPTIONS are this trade's: a Painter General pass-out ran a spray gun, a booth and an oven, not a lathe and a shaper.
